events.label: Bank of England decision — the second of three central bank decisions in three days
events.note: Added Sep 14 night: the Fed decides Wednesday, the BoE Thursday and the BoJ Friday. Three decisions inside three sessions is what turns a US energy shock into a global tightening impulse or leaves it domestic. The UK is importing the same crude: Brent above $108 with no Hormuz meeting scheduled.

events.label: August housing starts, weekly jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey - the first US activity data priced against the new projections
events.note: Added Sep 16 night: Lennar reported the same evening that its operating environment deteriorated as mortgage rates rose through the quarter, at roughly 6.8% on the thirty-year at quarter end, with new orders down 4% and the average sale price down to $371,000 from $389,000. Housing starts is the industry-wide check on whether that is company-specific or the shape of the sector at a funds rate the committee now projects at 4.1% through 2027.

events.label: Bank of Japan policy decision — markets pricing a September hike after Deputy Governor Himino flagged upside inflation risks
events.note: Added Sep 4 morning: the yen reached 155.28 per dollar on Sep 3, its strongest in a month, on BOJ hike bets rather than on the Fed alone. The decision lands two days after the Sep 15-16 FOMC, so the funding currency behind a large share of global duration positioning reprices twice inside four sessions. A yen driven by Japanese tightening keeps appreciating on a hot US print as well as a soft one; USD/JPY back above 158 would say the BOJ leg was overstated.

events.label: Rescheduled Iran-Gulf Hormuz meeting — NO date announced; Sep 18 is an indicative marker, not a scheduled event
events.note: Added Sep 14 morning: Oman postponed the Sep 14 Salalah meeting at Saudi Arabia's request and set no replacement date. Until one is announced there is no scheduled event that can take war premium out of crude, and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline — roughly 5M b/d to the Red Sea — is still shut after the Sep 10-11 drone strikes from Iraq. A WTI settle back below $100 would say the premium is deflating without a framework; above $105 puts a second month of energy pass-through into the data the Fed sees after Wednesday. Updated Sep 14 night: still no date. Brent ran above $109 intraday to about $108.15 and WTI to roughly $102.64, between the $100 and $105 settles this entry named. The dislocation to watch is that XLE reversed from up 1.2% premarket to down 0.94% at the close on that rally, with utilities off 1.34%.

events.label: Quarterly options expiration — the largest expiry of the quarter, landing the session after the Fed and on the Bank of Japan decision
events.note: Added Sep 15 night: the VIX fell to 17.10 from 17.29 on a session the S&P 500 lost 0.45%, so positions are being reduced into the decision rather than hedged. Expiry two days later removes whatever gamma is pinning the index, which is why the days after a Fed meeting that falls in expiry week often move more than the meeting itself.

events.label: Flash September PMIs (US, euro zone, UK) — the first broad activity reading covering the period since crude cleared $100
events.note: Added Sep 15 night: Empire State fell thirteen points to 7.6 with prices paid at 63.1 on responses collected September 2-10, before the pipeline outage fully priced. The flash PMIs say whether that was a regional print or the shape of the whole quarter, and their own prices-paid components are the first post-hike read on whether energy is reaching output prices.

events.label: Anthropic public S-1 expected — risk factors are the first document pricing the company's own call for slower capability growth
events.note: Added Sep 14 night: the filing precedes a mid-October roadshow supporting a listing valued at up to $2 trillion, with Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan leading. It lands weeks after CEO Dario Amodei argued publicly for slowing the rate at which model capabilities improve — a statement that on Sep 14 cost Marvell 6.00%, the Kospi 3.26% and SoftBank 10%, while cybersecurity rose 13-15%. The same session identified Anthropic as the customer behind a six-year, $13.7 billion compute contract, so the argument and the spending are not yet in conflict. The S-1 language is where they have to be reconciled in writing.

events.label: Final September consumer sentiment — confirms or revises the 4.6% year-ahead inflation expectation
events.note: Added Sep 11 night: the preliminary reading jumped six tenths to 4.6% on a survey period dominated by $100 crude and record retail diesel, and revisions to this series have been large in both directions this year. A final reading holding at or above 4.6% makes the expectations move structural; a revision back toward 4.2% makes it an energy artifact the committee can discount in November.

events.label: US import bans on Canadian dairy, motorcycles and alcoholic beverages take effect
events.note: Follows Canada's 15%-50% retaliatory tariffs on ~$20B of US goods (Sept 8) and the removal of Canadian-origin products from federal schedules worth $50B+ a year. A cost-push input running alongside $100 crude.

events.label: Saudi East-West pipeline restart window — shut since Sep 11, described as mostly out of service for weeks, with repairs estimated at three to five weeks
events.note: Added Sep 15 morning: the 1,200 km line carries roughly 4 million barrels a day from Abqaiq to Yanbu and was the workaround for the Hormuz blockade, so its loss removes the escape route rather than adding a second problem. About 4% of global supply is at risk and the kingdom could exhaust exportable oil within days. Sep 30 is an indicative marker, not an announced restart date. A confirmed restart is the single event that takes WTI back under $100 without any diplomacy behind it, and it is the input currently setting the long end of the Treasury curve. Updated Sep 15 night: WTI cleared $105 for a 4.7% gain to $106.12 and Brent rose 3% to $108.88 on reports the kingdom cancelled some European crude cargoes — WTI outrunning Brent narrowed the spread on a Gulf supply shock, which reads as physical tightness rather than headline risk. Refined-product costs reach the CPI basket with a four-to-six-week lag, putting this week's barrel in the November data rather than October's. Updated Sep 16 morning: WTI fell 1.29% to $104.46 and Brent 1.02% to $107.64 on an unexpected build in US crude inventories — the first decline in a week, and the first move down that came from supply arithmetic rather than diplomacy. The outage is unchanged, so the loss has been offset rather than resolved; a return above $105 would say the build was a weekly artifact.

events.label: Third-quarter bank earnings open - the test of whether Sep 16's regional selloff was deposit betas or positioning
events.note: Added Sep 16 night: on the day of the hike the SPDR S&P Bank ETF fell 2.6%, its worst session since February 27, with Huntington Bancshares down 5.6% and Citizens Financial 4.8% against JPMorgan's roughly 1%. A four-to-five-times gap between regional and money-center names prices deposit competition and credit at a 4.1% funds rate held through 2027, not net interest margin. Mid-October results either show that in deposit betas and provisions or they do not. The date is indicative of the usual opening week.

events.label: Anthropic IPO roadshow opens (indicative) — potentially the largest listing in history at up to $2T, days ahead of the November midterms
events.note: Added Sep 14 night: the date is indicative, not scheduled — the timeline moved from September to mid-October at the earliest. A $2 trillion debut would eclipse SpaceX's $1.77 trillion June 2026 listing. The supply side of the AI trade absorbing an offering that size, into a long end that touched 5% on the ten-year in September, is the test no earnings print delivers.

events.label: October FOMC decision (indicative date) - the first test of whether market pricing converges on the 4.1% median or the dots get discounted
events.note: Added Sep 16 night: the date is indicative pending the published Fed table. Market pricing entered Sep 16 charging roughly 41 bp of total 2026 tightening including that day's 25 bp; the September projections imply another full quarter point this year and no easing through 2027, and 16 of 18 officials see at least one more increase. October pricing moved to roughly 50% by the close. A ten-year back under 4.94% with October odds falling toward 25% would say the press-conference repricing was a one-session reaction; a hold above 5.04% would say the market has accepted 4.1% held for five more quarters.

events.label: US midterm elections — Trump's pledged $5,000 per-adult 'dividend' is contingent on Republicans holding both chambers
events.note: Pointed at about $154.5B of tariff revenue in the first ten months of FY2026; even 100 million recipients would cost $500B. The House is currently projected to go to the Democrats, so it is a tail input — but it lands on a long end that spent September repricing term premium.

events.label: Treasury expanded long-end buyback program ends — ops of at least $4B run from September 9
events.note: The count of completed operations is what separates absorbed supply from purchased calm at the long end. Updated Sep 10 night: the 30Y cleared 5.33%, August 18's prior high, and closed at 5.37% — its highest since 2007 — while the program was buying that maturity. The 2007 peak is 5.44%.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
